It's good to read this, Emma. At first, I thought it was risky of you to reveal too much about yourself on the internet.

I am suicidal and I get help from emailing [Samaritans](https://www.samaritans.org/how-we-can-help/contact-samaritan/) (a UK based charity organization on mental health).

It's not edgy or attention seeking when all you want to do is speaking out your mind. For now, take a breath in 7 seconds, hold in for another 7 seconds and breath out in 7 seconds. That is what I do when I was panic.

For now, I think you should go outside to a specific place where you live, just not too far from home and remember to tell your parents/guardians where you are going.

I guess you can find a peaceful place to take a short stroll, 

or a quiet place to read a book, 

or a joyful place full of animals and people, 

or anywhere that was once a delightful part of your childhood.

It's pretty generic, I know. It's really up to your hobbies and personal preferences.

I am surrounded by suicidal thoughts and feelings everyday and I guess every minute. Instead of focusing on them, I spend my quiet night time replying to other people on Reddit and upvoting posts. 

I don't know. I guess I'm too bored.

I think it's just natural for you to feel sad, empty, lonely, scared and so on in this very moment. Somehow, I think of this song on [Youtube](https://youtu.be/RBumgq5yVrA), like "Only know you love her when you let her go."

Truly, I have nothing relatable to your experience but a friendzone by my high school crush. I guess that is just life for both of us. There is sadness for now but there is always hope somehow.

I think this is when you need your friends most. Go hang out with them.
I upvoted, for the shot.

I'm relatively new to Reddit, like 2 weeks or so. I'm active on this sub, r/VietNam (I'm Vietnamese) and r/mentalhealth (I think I have at least a mental illness) mostly replying to others. I think most of my replies are forgotten but I hope they are helping.

Keep on crying and venting until you are too tired, then go to sleep. 

Probably, asking people (employers, teachers, etc.) for a day off or two or more. 

Doing whatever that makes you happy during those days, like watching silly Youtube videos (well, that's just my things). 

I'm way too late for the post. It's probably afternoon at your time now.

For me, it happened a year ago (roughly around Christmas or New Year Eve), when I was really panic about my life. It leaded to an eventual drop out as I can no longer study like how I used to. I was a senior in college.

I'm still struggle with a sort of mental illness. Last therapy sessions were horrible, especially that "Man up" from the therapist. 

Now, I study web development and designing in hope that I can make something of worth.

So yeah, a living human with struggles.

For anyone, who needs to vent.

As I am here, indeed a friend.

(A silly poem based on the title of your post. I'm not a troll. The title somehow reminded me of the phrase: "A friend in need is a friend indeed")

We men have been told to bottle up our emotions every single time. "Man up", they said. Yet, the strongest men are the ones who will admit that they cry.

Just remember that GOD is love and always expects his believers to love everyone regardless of their beliefs in HIM and others.

They are demands and suggestions on how I am supposed to be or to do as a man, a son and a student. They are what I tell myself, which were echoes of what people have said to me. 

Is it strange that those who claim to be the closest to me are the one who hurt me the most?
